question: The only Sugar normaly absorbed in the intestine against a concentration gradient is :
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Xylose" -> "passive diffusion" -> "along concentration gradient" -> "no active transport" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Mannose" -> "passive diffusion" -> "along concentration gradient" -> "no active transport" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Ribose" -> "passive diffusion" -> "along concentration gradient" -> "no active transport" -> 60%
analysis: The absorption of sugars in the intestine can occur via passive diffusion or active transport. Glucose is unique among the common dietary sugars because it is absorbed against its concentration gradient through active transport. This process is mediated by the sodium-glucose linked transporter 1 (SGLT1), which uses the sodium gradient to facilitate glucose uptake into the intestinal cells. This mechanism is well-documented and widely accepted in physiological studies. In contrast, other sugars like xylose, mannose, and ribose are absorbed through passive diffusion, which does not involve moving against a concentration gradient. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge and the enhanced information provided, glucose is the only sugar absorbed in this manner.
